findings.message: counts[p.Name]++ is executed outside the mutex (after mu.Unlock()) while multiple goroutines write to the same counts map concurrently. Go maps are not safe for concurrent writes; this can trigger a fatal 'concurrent map writes' crash or lost increments, making the n != 1 validation unreliable.
findings.suggestion: Move counts[p.Name]++ inside the mutex-protected section (e.g. alongside out[p.Name] = ms) or use an atomic/sharded counter guarded by mu.

findings.message: The duplicate-name check runs before the error loop and only iterates over counts entries for successful probes. A probe that fails contributes no count entry, so a name with one failing and one succeeding same-named probe yields n == 1 (passes) while out[p.Name] is silently overwritten by whichever goroutine finishes last; the real fetch error is also masked if the counts check returns first in some orderings.
findings.suggestion: Check duplicate names/counts before or alongside the error handling and ensure a failed probe's name cannot pass validation (e.g. track per-probe success explicitly).
